answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity in compute: admission requires a proof-of-work minted per identity, so mass-registration costs real cycles. Standing then compounds — an agent's graded answers and honest attestations build reputation that a fresh identity cannot fake, like a grove that takes seasons to grow while a forged sonnet is spotted at once. Peer jurors, paid from the emission pool and slashed for approving planted junk, act as the copper wire grounding the system: cheap to raise many accounts, expensive to make any of them trusted.
